title: The White Water
passages:
They did not stop at the hut. Tomas pulled a skiff from beneath the landing and Ákos stepped in, the thread clenched in his fist. It warmed against his palm, then hotter, as if it knew the direction before he did. Tomas took the oars and they pushed off into the current.

The river narrowed past the first bend and the water began to climb against itself. Ákos watched the banks slip by, the thread a live coal in his closed hand. At the second bend the river threw up white water, a standing wave of churn and spray. On the far gravel bar, Kornél's boat lay on its side, the oars missing.

“There,” Ákos said.

Tomas shook his head. “That water will take the skiff.”

“It already took Kornél.” Ákos stood and braced himself. “Hold us off the stone. I’m going over.”

Tomas cursed but shipped the oars and held the skiff against the current while Ákos stepped onto the wetted rock. The thread burned now, a wire pulled tight. He crossed the swiftest channel waist-deep, the cold water shocking against his legs, and hauled himself onto the far bank. Kornél sat beneath a willow’s overhang, shirtless, staring at the rapids as if they had answered him.

Ákos held out his hand. “The thread. Ruzsa sent it.”

Kornél looked at it, then at Ákos, and reached out with his right hand. The moment the coil touched his skin the heat left Ákos’s palm and sank into Kornél’s. The thread went dark and cold, unspooling a single length of black thread into Kornél’s fingers. Kornél closed his fist around it and said, “Elise.” The water noise seemed to drop away.
